title_en: Jiangxi Tengrong Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Bank of Jiangxi Co., Ltd., Nanchang High-tech Branch — dispute over a contract for assignment of creditor's rights

full_text_en:
Jiangxi Tengrong Industrial Co., Ltd. v. Bank of Jiangxi Co., Ltd., Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch — dispute over creditor's rights transfer agreement

Ruling Summary

Where a borrower and a lending bank, outside of the loan contract signed between them, separately enter into an agreement on creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management, stipulating that the borrower shall acquire the bank's creditor's rights and pay a certain amount of creditor's rights transfer fees without obtaining any benefits, it shall be determined that such agreement on creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management is intended to collect loan interest in a disguised form, among other purposes. The conduct of both parties in signing such agreement on creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management is carried out under a false declaration of intent and shall be found invalid in accordance with the law; the validity of the conduct of collecting interest hidden by such conduct shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 7094

Re-Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jiangxi Tengrong Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 301, Unit 2, Building 2, No. 297, Jiefang Road, Changling Town, Xinjian District, Nanchang City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Xiong Shenwu, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Authorized Litigation Representative: Wan Yinyun, lawyer of Jiangxi Jinghui Law Firm.

Authorized Litigation Representative: Yuan Yan, lawyer of Jiangxi Jinghui Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Bank of Jiangxi Co., Ltd., Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch, domiciled at Fengyuan Intelligent Building, No. 188, Huoju Avenue, Nanchang High-tech Development Zone, Jiangxi Province.

Person in Charge: Zhang Yu, President of the sub-branch.

The re-applicant, Jiangxi Tengrong Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tengrong Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court regarding the dispute over creditor's rights transfer contract with the respondent, Bank of Jiangxi Co., Ltd., Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch), dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2020) Gan Min Zhong No. 267 rendered by the Jiangxi High People's Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, and the review has now been concluded.

Tengrong Company applied for retrial on the grounds that: This case falls under the circumstances specified in Items 2 and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and a retrial should be granted. The main facts and reasons are as follows: (1) The second-instance judgment made errors in finding the basic facts. 1. The second-instance judgment erroneously found the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement" involved in the case to be legal and valid. This "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement" was forged; it was neither lawfully signed nor took effect, nor was it actually performed; moreover, it did not represent Tengrong Company's true declaration of intent, and thus has no legal effect. 2. The second-instance judgment erroneously found that the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" involved in the case had been fully performed. Tengrong Company had fully performed its obligations under the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and paid the full creditor's rights transfer price of RMB 10,620,439.51. However, Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch did not transfer the creditor's rights documents to Tengrong Company as agreed, but instead filed a lawsuit and applied for enforcement in its own name, constituting a fundamental breach of contract. Now, the debtor Jiangxi Weicai Industrial Co., Ltd. and the guarantor Jiangxi Nanfa Industrial Co., Ltd. have had their business licenses revoked by the industrial and commercial department and are unable to repay their debts. Tengrong Company is unable to assert rights against the debtor and the guarantor, and the contractual purpose of acquiring the creditor's rights involved in the case cannot be realized. (2) The second-instance judgment erroneously dismissed Tengrong Company's claims. The second-instance judgment's erroneous findings on the aforementioned basic facts led to an erroneous outcome, seriously damaging Tengrong Company's lawful rights and interests.

Upon review, this Court holds: The "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement" signed between Tengrong Company and Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch are, in name, agreements on creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management, but in substance, they are part of the loan contract for a principal amount of RMB 54,000,000 entered into by the parties. The reasons are as follows: First, from the content of the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement," it can be seen that the terms of these two agreements are not in line with common sense. Generally speaking, as the transferee of the creditor's rights and the entrusted manager of the assets, Tengrong Company should aim to obtain benefits by acquiring the creditor's rights and entrusting Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch to collect them. However, the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement" signed by the parties in this case stipulated that Tengrong Company would acquire Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch's creditor's rights at a consideration of RMB 10,620,439.51, and then entrust Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch to collect them. After deducting expenses, all remaining funds collected would belong to Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch as entrusted management fees. That is, after paying RMB 10,620,439.51 in creditor's rights transfer fees to Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch, Tengrong Company could not obtain any benefits from the acquired creditor's rights. Second, from the purpose of signing the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement," Tengrong Company did so to enter into a loan contract with Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch in order to obtain a loan of RMB 54,000,000 from it; Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch did so to collect an additional RMB 10,620,439.51 beyond the loan contract and to achieve the purpose of stripping non-performing assets, i.e., the creditor's rights involved in the case. In the "Report on Request for Provision of Debtor Information and Materials" submitted by Tengrong Company to Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch on May 13, 2015, it stated: "In order to obtain a loan of RMB 54,000,000 from your bank, our company accepted the conditions for the transfer of non-performing loan creditor's rights of your bank's debtor Jiangxi Weicai Industrial Co., Ltd...." Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch also stated during the first-instance trial: "For this loan, Tengrong Company enjoyed a preferential interest rate policy, with an annual interest rate of only 6.15%. At that time, the loan interest rate standard implemented by Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch was an annual interest rate of about 13%. This was also the reason why Tengrong Company agreed to accept the creditor's rights involved in this case." Third, from the actual performance of the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement," Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch did not actually perform these two agreements. Article 2 of the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" stipulated that Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch should transfer the creditor's rights and ancillary rights involved in the case to Tengrong Company on the closing date, i.e., October 28, 2013. However, based on the facts admitted by Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch during the first-instance trial, after receiving the creditor's rights transfer payment of RMB 10,620,439.51 from Tengrong Company, it did not transfer the creditor's rights to Tengrong Company but instead continued to pursue the creditor's rights in its own name by filing a lawsuit and applying to the court for compulsory enforcement. Moreover, Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch did not provide evidence to prove that it had informed Tengrong Company of the progress of the creditor's rights recovery. From the above comprehensive analysis, it can be seen that Tengrong Company's and Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch's declarations of intent regarding the creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management were false. The RMB 10,620,439.51 in creditor's rights transfer fees collected by Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch should be determined as interest collected in addition to the RMB 54,000,000 loan under the "Loan Contract" signed by the parties on October 21, 2013. Article 146 of the General Provisions of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A civil juristic act performed by a person with the counterparty based on a false declaration of intent shall be null and void. The validity of the civil juristic act concealed by the false declaration of intent shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws." Pursuant to this legal provision, the act of creditor's rights transfer and asset entrusted management performed by Tengrong Company and Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch based on a false declaration of intent in this case should be null and void. The act of paying the RMB 10,620,439.51 in loan interest concealed by the false declaration of intent is actually part of the civil juristic act of entering into a loan contract for a principal amount of RMB 54,000,000 between the parties. The validity of this act shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws. Given that Tengrong Company did not raise corresponding claims regarding the loan contract for the principal amount of RMB 54,000,000 entered into by the parties in this case, this Court does not review or determine the validity of that loan contract. Although the second-instance judgment's finding that the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and the "Asset Entrusted Management Agreement" were legal and valid was inappropriate, its dismissal of Tengrong Company's claims for rescission of the "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement" and for Bank of Jiangxi Nanchang High-tech Sub-branch to return the creditor's rights transfer payment and corresponding interest was not improper.

In conclusion, the grounds for retrial raised by Tengrong Company cannot be established, and its application for retrial does not meet the circumstances specified in Items 2 and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Paragraph 1 of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Paragraph 2 of Article 395 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court rules as follows:

The application for retrial by Jiangxi Tengrong Industrial Co., Ltd. is dismissed.
